newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal PM says budget plan untouchable.
newsitem.headline: Portugal PM says budget plan untouchable.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Monday that the 1997 budget his minority government will send to parliament cannot be changed, hinting that he would resign rather than see it watered down.
"I don't believe that any political group wants to distort this budget unless they intend, they themselves, to govern with their own budget," he told journalists.

The Socialists, who are four seats short of an outright majority in the 230-seat parliament, will send their budget plan to the legislature on Tuesday after it has been given final approval by the cabinet.
The programme sets down a budget deficit for next year which is inside the limit established by the European Union for membership of a planned single currency, along with a tough goal on inflation.
The government has made qualifying for economic and monetary union (EMU), due to start up in 1999, its top policy priority.
The budget plan, a draft outline of which was shown to members of parliament on Friday, will be discussed again by the cabinet later on Monday.

The main opposition party, the Social Democrats, has already said that it would not be prepared to see the government fall over the budget. Party leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa said his party would abstain in a budget vote if the alternative were a political crisis.
The government has warned that passing the economic test for EMU leaves no room for wage rises significantly in excess of inflation, predicted at 2.25-2.50 percent for next year.
It has offered the country's 500,000 public sector employees rises of 2.38 percent. But union leaders have dismissed the offer as "provocative."

Guterres said, however, that Portugal's public sector workers were being offered much more than in France or Spain where governments have decreed salary freezes to help them meet single currency economic targets.
